Import a measurement record from a long table

Source: R/record-import.R
measure_record_from_long.Rd

measure_record_from_long() turns an already parsed long table into a relational analytical record. Explicit column mappings define sample, injection, detector channel, curve, axis, and signal identity. Identifier and label columns must already be character vectors; values are not inferred from their appearance, and units are retained only as declarations.

Usage

measure_record_from_long(data, columns, source_id, allow_extra_columns = FALSE)

Arguments

data

A data frame containing one row per point in long form.

columns

A named character vector mapping canonical fields to existing input column names. Required names are sample_id, injection_id, channel_id, curve_id, location, and value. Optional names are channel_name, axis_name, axis_unit, value_name, and value_unit. Input columns cannot be reused for different fields.

source_id

A caller-declared, nonblank character source identifier.

allow_extra_columns

Set to TRUE to ignore input columns not named in columns.

Value

A measure_record containing samples, injections, channels, curves, and one source declaration.

Details

Curves and related entities retain first-appearance order. Points retain their occurrence order within each curve, including interleaved curves. Each curve may have its own finite, strictly monotone location grid. Values must be finite numeric values or NA; locations must be finite numeric values. The function does not sort points, infer missing metadata from other rows, infer units, or perform locale conversion. Conflicting declarations, including missing-versus-known mixtures within an entity, are errors. Its source record contains the caller-declared source_id only; this conversion does not compute a source digest or claim a complete transformation history.

Unmapped input columns are errors by default. Set allow_extra_columns = TRUE to explicitly ignore them. This API handles one-dimensional measurement curves. It does not import nD data, DAD/MS vendor structures, or vendor-specific file formats.

Examples

long_data <- tibble::tibble(
  sample_id = c("sample-01", "sample-01"),
  injection_id = c("injection-01", "injection-01"),
  channel_id = c("uv", "uv"),
  curve_id = c("curve-01", "curve-01"),
  location = c(250, 251),
  value = c(0.02, NA_real_)
)
long_columns <- c(
  sample_id = "sample_id",
  injection_id = "injection_id",
  channel_id = "channel_id",
  curve_id = "curve_id",
  location = "location",
  value = "value"
)
record <- measure_record_from_long(long_data, long_columns, "source-01")
record
#> <measure_record>
#>   Samples: 1
#>   Injections: 1
#>   Channels: 1
#>   Curves: 1
#>   Sources: 1
